blockers.summary: The round-26 repair to the 5-10-5 floor sentence replaced a true-but-wrong-direction reason with a reason that misstates the enzyme requirement the paper itself prints two pages earlier: ten is the TOP of the reported seven-to-ten range, not more than it.
blockers.quote: At 5-10-5 pairing the whole gap already demands ten base pairs, more than the seven-to-ten the enzyme is reported to need, so a shorter run that could still license cleavage goes uncounted and that last figure is a floor; the deposit gives the series.
blockers.evidence: The paper's own Introduction at the pin: 'Its length requirement is reported as a DNA gap of at least six nucleotides, with seven to ten the working range;<sup>13</sup><!--PMID:24981949-->'. The deposited literature record research/manuscripts/aso/lit-targets-aso-gap-length.json, record PMID 24981949, quotes[1].fragment: 'DNA gap size between 7 and 10 nucleotides is optimal', context_verbatim '...Frieden et al. concluded that a DNA gap size between 7 and 10 nucleotides is optimal for LNA/DNA/LNA antisense gapmers.' The deposited generator research/modalities/aso_parent_gap_pairing.py says it in terms on the line that defines the threshold: 'TEN IS THE STRICT END of that range'. Ten is therefore inside the reported range, at its upper bound; it is not 'more than' it. The floor DIRECTION survives (the reported minimum is six-to-seven, so runs of seven to nine could license cleavage and are uncounted at 5-10-5) — only the comparison is wrong. Present in the rendered outgoing copy: pdfminer extraction of fusion-junction-aso-journal-article-preprint.pdf contains 'more than the seven- to-ten the enzyme is reported to need'; all four PDF build stamps and both docx stamps record built_from aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md = 7d22f98b..., the pinned digest, so every deliverable carries it.
blockers.why_a_reader_would_be_misled: A reader is told the screen's threshold at the longest geometry sits ABOVE everything the literature reports the enzyme to need, i.e. that the criterion is strictly more conservative than any reported requirement. It is not: it sits exactly at the top of the cited optimal range, and the paper says so itself in the Introduction. The reader therefore over-reads how much margin the 25.4% figure has as a floor, and meets two incompatible statements of the same cited fact in one paper.
blockers.artifact: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md (Results, gap-length paragraph) — and, rebuilt from it, fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.pdf, -manuscript.pdf, -preprint.pdf, -anonymized.pdf, -manuscript.docx
blockers.proposed_replacement: At 5-10-5 pairing the whole gap already demands ten base pairs, the strict end of what the enzyme is reported to need, so a shorter run that could still license cleavage goes uncounted and that last figure is a floor; the deposit gives the series.

blockers.summary: The repair that cut the five-step enumeration replaced it with a one-clause summary that is wrong about the cited framework: steps 4 and 5 are risk assessment and risk management, not laboratory steps, as the deposit's own verbatim record of that framework states.
blockers.quote: An industry working group's 2025 off-target recommendations<sup>14</sup><!--PMID:39912803--> set five steps, the first in silico and the rest in the laboratory.
blockers.evidence: research/manuscripts/aso/lit-targets-aso-instruments.json (deposited — it is entry-present in fusion-junction-aso-archive-manifest.json), supplementary_record_2026_08_31_the_five_step_framework_verbatim.record.five_steps_verbatim: 'The proposed workflow encompasses five key steps: (1) OffT identification throughcomplementarity prediction and transcriptomics analysis, (2) focus on cell types with relevant ONT activity, (3)verification and margin assessment, (4) risk assessment based on the OffT biological role, and (5) management of unavoidable OffTs.' The same record's what_the_paper_takes_from_it says it correctly: 'steps 2, 3, 4 and 5 are laboratory OR GOVERNANCE steps'. The manuscript's replacement flattens that to 'the rest in the laboratory', which is false of (4) and (5). Secondary, from the same cut: the deleted text named step 1's two components ('identification in silico with transcriptomics'), which is what gave the retained next clause 'the in-silico half of the first step' a referent; with the enumeration gone, 'the first in silico' and 'the in-silico half of the first step' sit in consecutive sentences with nothing telling the reader what the other half is. Present in the rendered outgoing copy: pdfminer extraction of the preprint PDF contains 'the first in silico and the rest in the laboratory'.
blockers.why_a_reader_would_be_misled: The paper locates its own scope against this framework, so what the framework's other four steps ARE is load-bearing for what the paper is conceding it has not done. A reader is told the remaining four are laboratory work; two of them are desk risk assessment and risk management, which no laboratory supplies. The paper's own deposited record of the source contradicts the sentence, so a reviewer who downloads the archive reads both.
blockers.artifact: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md (Introduction, final paragraph) — and, rebuilt from it, fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.pdf, -manuscript.pdf, -preprint.pdf, -anonymized.pdf, -manuscript.docx
blockers.proposed_replacement: An industry working group's 2025 off-target recommendations<sup>14</sup><!--PMID:39912803--> set five steps, the first in-silico prediction with transcriptomics. (nine words against thirteen, and it keeps the literal phrase 'the in-silico half of the first step' in the following sentence, which test_the_manuscript_asserts_the_relation_its_artifacts_compute.py anchors on.)

p1s.summary: The guard on the 5-10-5 floor sentence hard-asserts the erroneous wording as a literal string, so the correct wording fails the build and an editor is pushed back to the wrong sentence.
p1s.evidence: research/manuscripts/tests/test_journal_article_numbers.py at the pin: assert re.search(r"more than the seven-to-ten the enzyme is reported to need", flat), with a comment reading '...above the enzyme's reported seven-to-ten, so shorter licensing runs go uncounted.' The guard is right that the word 'floor' and its reason must travel together; it pins the wrong form of the reason. Fixing REG-1 requires this literal to move with it.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Any correct restatement of the comparison — 'the strict end of', 'the top of the reported range' — goes red while the wrong sentence stays green, which is the inverse of what the guard is for.
p1s.artifact: research/manuscripts/tests/test_journal_article_numbers.py (repository tooling, not in the outgoing set)

p1s.summary: Nothing binds the paper's one-sentence description of PMID 39912803's five steps to the deposited verbatim of those steps; the existing guard only forbids claiming MORE of them, and its own rationale repeats the error.
p1s.evidence: research/manuscripts/tests/test_the_manuscript_asserts_the_relation_its_artifacts_compute.py, row 'in-silico-half-of-the-first-step': it anchors on r"This work performs[^;]{0,140};", requires the literal 'the in-silico half of the first step', and forbids only 'all five of those steps|all five steps|each of the five steps|the whole of the first step|the first three steps|steps one to'. Nothing reads the clause that DESCRIBES the other four steps, and the row's own decided_by string says 'steps two to five of the cited recommendations (PMID:39912803) are laboratory steps' — the same mischaracterization REG-2 files, sitting in the guard that was supposed to police the sentence. The deposited verbatim exists (lit-targets-aso-instruments.json) and nothing compares the prose to it.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Any future rewrite of the framework summary — 'the rest in vitro', 'the rest experimental', 'four laboratory steps' — passes every guard, exactly as the current wrong clause does.

p2s.summary: The repaired genome-screen sentence replaced an explicit subject with a pronoun whose nearest antecedent is the contrast the genomic search itself produced, so the sentence now reads as denying its own preceding numbers.
p2s.evidence: At the pin: 'The genome-wide screen does not separate them: 156 hybridisable gap-paired sites against 135. It scans genomic sequence rather than transcripts, most of it never transcribed, so that contrast is not one the genomic search supports.' The prior text named the referent — 'the transcriptome contrast is not a difference the whole genome supports' — and the intended referent is still the transcriptome separation two sentences earlier (123 near-matches against eight; the EWSR1 precursor site the TAF15 reagent lacks). Read as written, 'that contrast' is 156-against-135, which the genomic search is precisely what produced. No number is wrong; the sentence is unparseable in the direction it means. Replacement of equal or shorter length: 'It scans genomic sequence rather than transcripts, most of it never transcribed, so the transcriptome contrast is not one it supports.' (20 words against 21.) Site: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md, reagents paragraph.

p2s.summary: The Tables sentence was repaired to name two sources, and that repair opened a contradiction with a DEPOSITED code file whose docstring still claims one — the fourth site of a defect that file's own inline comment records having been fixed three times.
p2s.evidence: The manuscript now reads 'generated from the canonical sequence file and, for the controls, from the screened-control record it is itself built from'. That is CORRECT and I verified it: research/manuscripts/aso_journal_tables.py::_controls() loads research/modalities/aso-control-oligos.json, and research/manuscripts/aso_sequence_manifest.py line 565 loads the same file, so the canonical CSV is itself built from it. But the same deposited module's docstring still reads '⚠ THIS GENERATOR READS THE CANONICAL SEQUENCE FILE AND NOTHING ELSE, by design. Every cell it emits is a column of `fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv` ... The one exception is the test-article map below' — one exception where there are two. The module's own comment at ~line 201 already records the miss: '`_controls` reads `aso-control-oligos.json`. Nobody had noticed the last one in three rounds of getting this sentence wrong.' aso_journal_tables.py IS in fusion-junction-aso-archive-manifest.json, so a reader who downloads the archive gets the paper's sentence and the module's contradiction of it. Per the brief this is a P2: it does not contradict a number the paper prints, falsify a manifest promise, or misdescribe what the archive contains.
